title: a task that regenerates a published page can record a green gate before its commit, and a journal row keeps every detail its writer passed
desiredOutcome: The pre-commit sweep compares published pages against a fresh render, and the comparison against what the commit carries runs where a commit exists (CI and verify.sh --release), so a task regenerating a page is gated green on correct work without an override; close-phase's phase.merged row carries its parent, and a detail key outside the journal's allow-list at any append site fails the build instead of being dropped.

tasks.title: the published-page check compares against a fresh render before the commit and against the commit only where one exists
tasks.description: F521 (quality-gates-internal PLAN.md). ra23's live arm (--selftest compares every published page against HEAD) sits in the pre-commit sweep, so a task that regenerates a page with the repo's own recipe is red by construction until its commit, and commit-task-work binds a commit to a green gate - P80.7, P80.15 and P80.20 went through --override-verdict. Keep the fresh-render comparison in the pre-commit sweep; move the vs-commit comparison to where a commit exists - the CLI run CI and verify.sh --release make - and state in CONTRIBUTING.md and verify.sh which set carries it. gate-parity.py must stay green (every description of the gate set agrees). Red-first: a fixture page that matches a fresh render and not HEAD makes the selftest red on the current code and green after; allow: a page matching neither a fresh render nor HEAD still fails the pre-commit sweep, and the vs-commit arm still fails on a page the commit does not carry.

tasks.title: the git-call recorder counts any root inside this checkout, and the ci.yml reader reads a call only from a literal block
tasks.description: Phase review round 3 (review-P87c.json). (1) The recorder flags a root only when it equals REPO; a subdirectory root still asks this checkout's HEAD (git -C REPO/tools resolves the same toplevel). Flag a root equal to or under REPO (realpath, then == or startswith(target + os.sep)); add a ra30b row with a subdirectory root. (2) Two YAML shapes read silently as a no-flag call, which is exactly ci.yml's expected answer: `run: > # comment` and a plain multi-line scalar with the flag on a continuation line. Structural rule: a call to the tool is read only from a single-line `run:` or a literal `|` block; any other run: with deeper-indented continuation lines that mentions the tool is refused by line, and the folded pattern allows a trailing comment. Add both shapes to ra29c. (3) The comment saying the file runs no git outside _git is wrong (fixture repos at _head_fixture and ra17); say it runs git outside _git only against fixture repos. Re-wrap the CHANGELOG line. Red first for 1 and 2.

tasks.title: the ci.yml reader accepts only the call shapes it can read and refuses every other line that names the tool
tasks.description: Phase review round 4 (review-P87d.json). The reader still reads every line naming the tool and only exempts blocks whose key is spelled exactly `run:`, so "run": >, 'run': >, `run : >`, `&k run: >` read silently as no-flag (ci.yml's expected answer), a quoted one-line value is dropped, and `run: &a |`, `run: !!str >` or a deeper comment under a one-line run: are refused with a wrong message. Invert the rule into an allow-list: in YAML mode a line naming the tool is accepted only as (a) a one-line `run:` (optionally after `- `) whose unquoted value is the call, or (b) a line in the body of a block opened by a plain `run: |` (optionally `|-`/`|+`, trailing comment allowed). Every other non-comment line that names the tool is refused by line with the two accepted shapes named. A full-line comment is never a call and never extends a value. Pin each review shape (quoted keys, spaced key, anchored key, quoted value, anchored/tagged indicator, deeper comment) in ra29d or a new case: each is either read correctly or refused, none read silently. Re-wrap the manifest-conventions.md phase.merged bullet. Red first.

tasks.title: the call reader reads block-scalar context and counts only a word in command position as the call
tasks.description: Phase review round 5 (review-P87e.json). Two silent misreads remain. (1) The YAML reader checks line shapes, not context: a `run: <call>` line inside another key's block scalar (a `- name: >` body, `with: script: |`) is read as a step call. Track every block scalar (any key whose value opens with | or > after optional anchor/tag/indicators) and its body by indentation; a body that is not an accepted plain `run: |` is opaque - a tool-naming line inside it is refused by line, never read. State the allow-list as over YAML context, and fix the CHANGELOG/comment. (2) Any word ending in the tool path counts as the call, so `ls <tool>`, `git diff -- <tool>`, `echo see <tool>` read as a no-flag call (ci.yml's expected answer). Count a word as the call only in command position: the command word itself, or the word right after a python interpreter word (python, python3, python3.N, an absolute path to one) with no other argument between; a mention anywhere else is not a call. Add fixtures for both, red first, in both readers (shell and YAML) where they apply.
